reason: The mapping to Articles 14, 26(2), and 26(5) of the EU AI Act provides a defensible and sufficiently complete regulatory basis. Article 14 establishes the general obligation for human oversight. Article 26(2) requires a procedure for human intervention, and Article 26(5) mandates a process for human review of high-risk AI system outputs. Together, these provisions support the availability of human review, rejection, stop, override, and escalation capabilities.
applicability_note: This assessment applies to high-risk AI systems as defined by the EU AI Act, which are decision-impacting and fall under the scope of the regulation's oversight requirements.
challenge_comment: The challenge is to ensure that the specific control mechanisms (review, rejection, stop, override, escalation) are not just theoretically available but are effectively implemented and documented as part of the system's operational procedures and governance.
